name: Inha University
overview:
Inha University is a private university located in Incheon, South Korea, traditionally known for research and education in engineering and physical science. The university was established by the first president of South Korea in 1954. The university is the result of cooperation between South Korea and the United States. It is ranked the 10th university in Korea and 4th in the field of Engineering and Science.


Inha University has 12 faculties in the fields of Natural Sciences, Engineering, Economics and Commerce, Business and Administration etc.


The campus is a half hour drive from Incheon International Airport and an hour and a half drive from Seoul.
administrative:
1. Application Dossier


You will be working directly with the partner university regarding your application. You will receive an email from Inha University to create your user session and apply online.


Your host university may ask for the following documents:

  • Photo (JPG format)
  • Letter of recommendation (use the template provided by Inha University)
  • Housing Application Form (use the template provided by Inha University)
  • Transcripts (available on intra)
  • Copy of passport
  • Financial proof (bank certificate of min. $8,000 for one year of study in Korea, the issuance day, account holder’s full name, balance of account, the signature of the bank) in English and a family relations certificate if you are not the holder of the bank account (translated in English)
  • Certificate of English level (Tepitech): available on intra
  • Certificate of Enrollment: available on intra


To be given to Epitech campus administration:

  • Addendum to the contract
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier


This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


2. Acceptance Letter

Once your application has been accepted by Inha University you will receive the necessary documents to apply for a visa:

  • Certificate of Admission
  • Letter of Acceptance
  • Certificate of Business Registration


3. Visa and ARC (more information here and here)


You will have to apply for a D-2-6 visa.


If you are French, all applications must be submitted to the Korea Visa Application Center (KVAC). If you are not French, additional documents might be required. (Some documents can be prepared in advance.)


Visa application particularities:

  • Price in 2025 (application fee + visa fee + optional postal delivery ): about 126€
  • If you live in France, the visa application documents must be sent to Paris by registered mail (enveloppe en recommandé). IMPORTANT: The original passport must be sent, not a copy
  • There is NO in-person meeting at KVAC or the Embassy for this process


How do you collect your documents? (2 options):

  • Pay additional mailing costs to receive the visa and passport to the address indicated on the KVAC Waiver Courier document (delivered by La Poste Registered Mail Service)
  • OR
  • Apply by mail and collect them on-site at KVAC Paris after being contacted by KVAC


From 30 days after your arrival, you must apply for the Alien Registration Card (ARC), the identification card necessary for any stay longer than 90 days. This is a Korean official procedure; Keimyung will assist you when the semester begins.

  • Cost: about 20€
  • Issuance time: Approx. 2 months (you cannot leave the country before receiving the card)
  • You should always carry your ARC with you (you need it to open a bank account, ID checks, online shopping, etc.)
  • Important: You cannot leave South Korea and travel around Asia without your ARC – it is essential to exit the country.


4.Insurance and Health


It is imperative that you take out insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student. To take out international insurance, the market is quite open.


Please click here for more information.


When you receive your ARC, a Korean insurance account will automatically be created for you (approximately $70/month). You can choose to cancel and just count on your own international insurance, but please note that you will face disadvantages (deferred reimbursements, etc.).


If you choose to live in the dormitory on campus, a Tuberculosis (TB) Test result in English or Korean, taken within 4 weeks before the dormitory move-in date is also required. The test should include student’s name, hospital/clinic name, date of the test, and test results in English/Korean. The test can be conducted in Korea, and in the form of a skin test, blood test, or X-ray. You'll need to bring the original test result to the dormitory move-in.


For more information, you can consult the country’s health file at: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/coree-du-sud


Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.


5.Prepare your arrival


For advice to travelers issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs on the country, click here.

Please install KakaoTalk before arriving and bring cash.


6.Campus Life


Free shuttles offered by Inha University from the airport to the university. (3 dates available)


Inha buddy program is intended to promote different cultures and exchange between international students and Korean students. Every year, Inha buddies and international students make great memories together and continue their friendship over the border. Applicants for buddy program should click check box when applying for exchange program through the online application system.


You will benefit from a Football Field, a Gym facility etc., Various monthly cultural activities organized by ISL (International Student Lounge), Internet and scanner [location: student building 5F] available at ISL office, Language exchange and tutoring program
accomodation:
On-campus accommodation (more information here and here)


1. Woongbijae

"Woongbijae" , Dormitory 1, a five-story building with one basement level and five aboveground, can accommodate up to 1,010 students. In addition to regular Inha students, Woongbijae houses exchange students, and is fully accessible for handicapped students. Woongbijae also offers LAN access ports, satellite TV reception, DID telephones, and a computer room. Other facilities include a cafeteria, a laundry room, a small lounge area, providing students with a comfortable living environment.


2. Biryongjae

Inha University opened the new Dormitory 'Biryongjae' , resembling an undulating wave, outwardly appearing a design of nature in 2006. Accommodating over 1,150 students, the new 13 story dormitory is equipped with various modern facilities such as LAN connection, digital satellite receivers, and DID telephones. The dormitory also provides students with access to a fitness room, Internet Cafe and various welfare facilities.


Dormitory fees (as of Fall 2025): approx. USD 950-1000 per semester (including a meal per day)


Condition: quadruple rooms or double rooms


Payment can be made in cash upon arrival


Off-campus accommodation (more information here)


You can choose to live in a share house with roommates or in a studio.


There are a number of housing options around the school area and in Incheon. International students who are not living in the dormitory are recommended to go and see firsthand any housing before signing a contract.


If you need a help with finding off campus housing for your stay in Korea, you can contact the housing agency at https://www.stay14.com.


You can choose to live in Seoul but please not that it'll take you an hour and a half to go to Inha University.


Tips:

  • There have been many cases of foreigners being the targets of inflated rental prices and scams in Seoul. So be very careful and if possible, get a Korean friend to help you in your search.
  • In March 2004, Korean laws were changed and it became illegal for landlords to force foreigners to pay more than three months rent in advance.
  • Check to see if you have to buy official waste disposal bags, which are sold in local through out stores. They come in different sizes, and recyclable material should be put out separately. Different neighborhoods have different recycling systems.
courses:
Credits


You will need to validate 30 local credits in total, 15 per semester (each course is worth 3 local credits) to validate 60 ECTS of the international year.


Academic Calendar (more information here)


  • 1st semester: from September to January
  • 2nd semester: from early February until early June

Plan an arrival the last week of August to settle in & do the administrative procedures.


You will have to choose your classes as follows:

  • Option 1: 3 computer classes, 1 Korean class, 1 elective class (non-computer)
  • Option 2: 4 computer classes and 1 Korean class
  • Computer classes must be at the 3rd and 4th year level
  • Business classes, Korean language, and Korean culture classes are at the 1st year level



Department and Courses


You will need to register within the College of Engineering (Undergraduate), choose the Electrical and Electronic engineering or Integrated system engineering specializations (first and foremost for a wider course choice).


Class registration is on a first come, first served basis, often occurs early in the morning (European time) and fills up quickly due to limited space. We recommend staying awake or waking up early to secure your preferred classes.


The list of courses validated by Epitech is below:

  • Operating system
  • Information security
  • Business administration
  • Korean society and politics / Korean cultural through film
  • Basic Korean Language
  • Database design
  • Software engineering
  • Computer networks
  • IoT application system
  • Numerical analysis
  • Database
  • Maching learning
  • E-Business
  • IT and business
  • The analysis Study for Economic Problems
  • Enterpreneurship & social enterprise
  • Organizational behavior
  • Technology innovation & enterpreneurship
  • Embedded system
  • Mobile Communications
  • System programming
  • Capstone Design in ICT
  • Information and Coding Theory
  • Digital Image and Processing Design


Important notes

  • Presence in class is compulsory, under penalty of loss of visa and repatriation to France at the student's expense (impact on credits).
  • The courses are most likely more academic than at EPITECH.
  • The course list is given for information only. It can change from year to year.
  • If a course is not available when you arrive on site, EPITECH cannot be held responsible for it.
  • Any Tech 4 abroad involves an EIP! Take advantage of the free slots you will have to advance it.
cost:
Financial Overview (4th year Epitech)


  • You must pay the tuition fees for the 4th year of EPITECH, as well as the re-registration fees and related fees.
  • EPITECH covers the tuition fees.
  • The tuition supplement payable by you is indicated at the top of this page (if applicable).
  • Other costs at your expense include: travel, accommodation on site, insurance, and everyday expenses (books, food, transport, etc.).


Other Expenses


  • Roundtrip flights: from 800€
  • Visa: 126€
  • ARC: 20€
  • Insurance from university: 70€/month
  • Additional Insurance: 300-600€ for additional insurance contract depending on the coverage


Estimated Monthly Budget


The local currency is the Won. 1 € = 1667,19 KRW (rate as of October 2025).

Please check the Numbeo website to compare the cost of living between your city of origin and your city of exchange. Please note that everyone's budget will be different according to one's lifestyle.


You should plan a budget of about 600€ a month, excluding rent.


Housing (+utilities) : 1000€/semester for on-campus housing / 450€/month for off-campus housing with roommates


Food : maximum 300€


Transportation : Rechargeable T-money card: 35€ / In Seoul Metro: 0.7 to 1.20€ / Bus: 0.8 to 2€ / Monthly Climate card: 40€


Phone, internet / 12€ for unlimited 5G / Please note that if you’re with Free Mobile, their €20/month plan includes 35G data in South Korea / Former students (2024-2025) have recommended Chingu Mobile.


Leisure / 100€+


These prices are indicative and may vary.


Additional Information (specifics, advice, useful links, etc.)

  • Your visa allows you to work in South Korea up to 20 hours a week, Monday to Friday, during your study stay. However, to be able to work, you must change your visa to an S3 on site. Please note that it is still very difficult for a foreigner who does not speak Korean to find a part-time job.
  • Make sure to check the withdrawal rights abroad on your credit card before arriving, or use a card such as Revolut. You'll be able to create a bank account in South Korea only when you have your ARC.
  • Useful apps: Coupang and Karrot (online shopping - equivalents of Amazon and Leboncoin), KakaoTalk and Google Translate/Papago/Deepl (communication), Baemin and Ubereats (food delivery), Uber, Naevar/Kakao maps because Google maps doesn't work (transport)
  • Use the Kakao Subway app, very useful for navigating Seoul’s subway. You can buy a metro card at a 7/11 or C&U (your student or bank card may also be used after about a month).
  • It is not compulsory to get a SIM card, as free wifi is often available in the streets. However, SIM cards provide access to more wifi, especially in the subway.
  • Korean people don't really cook and, rather, eat out a lot. You have options like restaurants (like pochas) and convenience stores which are open 24/7. Food is less expensive than in France. Typically, people share a few dishes.
